examples.name: Presence badge
examples.description: Shows availability when no calendar status is present.

examples.name: Offline badge
examples.description: Uses the semantic subtle content color for the offline badge icon.

examples.name: Status wins over presence
examples.description: Renders accepted status badge instead of online presence badge.

examples.name: Disabled interactive avatar
examples.description: Suppresses interaction and applies disabled visual treatment without a badge combination.

examples.name: Selectable interactive avatar
examples.description: An avatar people pick: given isSelected, the button is a toggle with aria-pressed, and its name is "Ben Averill, busy" without the word selected.
examples.jsx: <Avatar name="Ben Averill" presence="busy" isInteractive isSelected={isPicked} onClick={togglePicked} />

examples.name: Translated status words
examples.description: The words Avatar adds to the accessible name are props with English defaults.

examples.name: Team/partner entity, no image
examples.description: entityType="team" swaps the fallback artwork to a two-person silhouette instead of the default individual one, for a firm or partner entity appearing alongside people.

examples.name: Photo with a name
examples.description: Give every avatar a name, even with a photo. It names the fallback when the photo fails.

examples.name: Decorative, beside a visible name
examples.description: decorative hides a static avatar from assistive technology when a visible name sits next to it.

antiExamples.name: Photo alone, no name
antiExamples.reason: The avatar has no accessible name, and a failed photo leaves an unnamed silhouette. Set name even when there's a photo.

antiExamples.name: State written into name
antiExamples.reason: Avatar already adds the badge word to the accessible name, so the state is read twice. Pass the plain name and let presence or status add it.

antiExamples.name: decorative on an interactive avatar
antiExamples.reason: decorative is ignored on an interactive avatar, and without a name the button is unnamed. Give it a name.

antiExamples.name: Several Avatars in a row for a group of people
antiExamples.jsx:
<Avatar name="Ben Averill" />
<Avatar name="Jordan Lee" />
<Avatar name="Sam Ortiz" />
antiExamples.reason: Several people together belong in Avatar Group, which overlaps them and counts the rest.
